name: Thaddaeus
bio: Lebbaeus, surnamed Thaddaeus, was one of the twelve apostles Jesus named and sent out with authority to heal and cast out demons, instructed to go first to Israel rather than Gentiles or Samaritans (Matthew 10:1-5). Luke's list of the Twelve names him instead "Judas, the brother of James" (Luke 6:16). At the Last Supper, Thaddaeus — distinguished in the text as "Judas... not Iscariot" — asked Jesus why he would reveal himself to the disciples but not to the world; Jesus answered that he would make his home with whoever loved him and kept his word (John 14:22-23).
